question: Which of the following fields is NOT covered by the National Eminence Award?

options.text: Music of all forms and origin

solution:
The correct answer is __**Literature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Eminence Award (also known as Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship) recognizes individuals for their contributions in **Theatre, Dance, and Music**.
 
• It is the highest honor conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• The award does not specifically cover the field of **Literature**, as it primarily focuses on the performing arts.
 
• Recipients of the award are selected for their exceptional dedication and lifelong achievements in their respective fields of performing arts.
 
• Fields such as **Music of all forms and origin**, Theatre, and Dance are prominently included in the scope of the award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**

 
 
• It is India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, established in 1953 by the Indian government.
 
• The Akademi aims to preserve and promote India's cultural heritage in performing arts.
 
• Apart from awards, it conducts research, documentation, and the publication of materials related to performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Fields of Recognition:**
 
 
• The awards focus on Theatre, Music (Hindustani, Carnatic, and folk traditions), and Dance (classical and traditional forms).
 
• It also includes allied performing arts, puppetry, and the contribution of scholars and teachers in these fields.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Award:**
 
 
• The award includes a citation, a memento, and a cash prize.
 
• It is one of the most prestigious recognitions for performing artists in India.
 
 
 
• **Notable Recipients:**
 
 
• Some legendary recipients include M.S. Subbulakshmi (Music), Rukmini Devi Arundale (Dance), and Habib Tanvir (Theatre).
 
• These individuals have contributed significantly to the preservation and global recognition of Indian performing arts.
